description:
Mission-Focus

A team leveraging machine learning and space physics to decode the complex behavior of zero-gravity fire and protect the next generation of space explorers. By transforming decades of NASA microgravity combustion experiments into intelligent analytics, we generate actionable, AI-driven insights for proactive fire prevention and mitigation. Together, we are engineering the life-safety systems needed to safeguard deep-space habitats on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
summary: As humanity prepares for sustained lunar habitats under Artemis (30% O2 at 10.2 psi) and six-month transits to Mars with no immediate rescue, spacecraft fire safety is a mission-critical priority. In microgravity and partial gravity, flames behave drastically differently than on Earth—forming dim, spherical, diffusion-limited fronts and invisible cool flames that challenge standard terrestrial sensors and flammability rules. While NASA has collected decades of microgravity combustion data across ISS experiments (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire, SAME, FLEX, ACME, SPICE, SLICE), the sheer volume of raw tables, sensor logs, and videos makes cross-experiment comparison difficult. We developed "Flame in Freefall," an interactive, Super Intelligence (SI)-powered decision-support dashboard that unifies, ranks, and interprets NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) combustion datasets. Users can select a target habitat (ISS, Moon Base, Pressurized Rover, Mars), filter by environmental conditions, inspect an auditable relevance ranking, compare material flammability across oxygen concentrations (21%, 30%, 100% O2), and generate uncertainty-aware fire risk predictions covering Prevention, Detection, and Suppression.
details:
• What It Does & How It Works: Flame in Freefall bridges the gap between raw NASA microgravity combustion experiments and actionable engineering decisions. It follows a five-step workflow (Select Habitat -> Set Conditions -> Review Ranked Results -> Open Experiment Detail -> Export Safety Guidance):
      1. Smart Search & Habitat Filter: Filters NASA PSI records by fuel/material (e.g., PMMA, cotton-fiberglass SIBAL fabric, droplets, gases), oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow speed, gravity regime (0g, Lunar 0.16g, Martian 0.38g, Earth 1g), and ISS hardware (MSG, CIR, DAFT, Cygnus).
      2. Auditable SI Ranking Engine: Scores and ranks matching experiments using a transparent weighted formula: Score = 0.40(Relevance) + 0.30(Evidence) + 0.20(Transfer) + 0.10(Confidence). Every recommendation traces directly back to its source NASA experiment.
      3. Side-by-Side Comparison View: Compares the same material across different atmospheres (21% O_2, 30% O_2, 100% O_2) or compares multiple materials under identical cabin conditions using interactive charts and experiment metadata.
      4. Physics-Bounded Risk Prediction: Uses 0g (ISS) and 1g (Earth) experimental bounds to interpolate fire behavior across the partial-gravity gap (0.16g Moon and 0.38g Mars), outputting a 0–100 Risk Score, estimated ignition delay, flame spread rate (mm/s), smoke/detector response lag, and explicit uncertainty bounds.
    • Benefits & Intended Impact: Transforms fragmented scientific logs from BASS/BASS-II, Saffire I–VI, SAME, FLEX, and ACME into an integrated Prevention + Detection + Suppression advisor for habitat designers, mission planners, and safety engineers working on the ISS, Lunar Gateway, Artemis Moon Base, Pressurized Rovers, and Mars transit vehicles. It also supports terrestrial fire safety applications in sealed environments like aircraft, submarines, and hospitals.
    • Tools, Coding Languages & Software: Python, Streamlit (interactive web dashboard), Pandas & NumPy (data normalization and physics-bounded interpolation), Plotly (interactive multi-variable visualizations), Scikit-learn (risk modeling & feature weighting), and LLM/SI API integration for natural-language synthesis of experiment findings.
    • Creativity & Team Considerations: Rather than treating AI/SI as a black box that might hallucinate safety-critical numbers, our team designed an auditable ranking and bounding methodology that explicitly shows confidence intervals, addresses the partial-gravity data gap until lunar experiments (LUCI/FM2) fly, and links every insight to verified NASA PSI records.
